title: Balarila: Deep Learning for Semantic Grammar Error Correction in Low-Resource Settings
authors: Espiritu, P.; Jadie, J.; Ponce, A.; Cheng, C.
venue: Proceedings of the First Workshop in SouthEast Asian Language Processing
tldr: Balarila achieves F0.5 of 70.75 for Filipino grammar error correction using GECToR-inspired deep learning with synthetic data, addressing semantic errors beyond lexical ones.
problem_and_motivation: Existing Filipino grammar checkers can only correct lexical errors. There is no publicly available Filipino grammar checker that addresses semantic errors, which are more complex.
approach: Builds Balarila, a deep learning-based Filipino GEC model inspired by GECToR approach.
Devises automated error generation pipeline creating synthetic datasets from online news sources.
Fine-tunes Tagalog BERT and RoBERTa models in two stages using generated corpus.
Evaluates using precision, recall, and F0.5 scores for GEC and multi-class confusion matrix for GED.
Three models: BERT Tagalog Base, RoBERTa Tagalog Base, and RoBERTa Tagalog Large.
findings: num: RoBERTa Tagalog Large achieved highest F0.5 score of 70.75.
num: RoBERTa Tagalog Base achieved F0.5 of 69.00, demonstrating cost-effectiveness.
RoBERTa-Large generally performed better than BERT-Base and RoBERTa-Base in GEC scores.
RoBERTa-Base had only 1.75% F0.5 score difference from RoBERTa-Large while using fewer resources.
